justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
